newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open much stronger after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open much stronger after U.S. data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened much stronger on Tuesday, matching sharp gains in U.S. Treasuries, which rallied after the release of weaker-than-expected U.S. economic data.

"They were very good numbers," said Rod Kerr, a bond portfolio manager with Laketon Investment Management. Kerr said the data has increased speculation that the U.S. Federal Reserve might not have to hike rates again when it meets in May.
Canada's 30-year benchmark rose C$1.60 to C$108.85 to yield 7.237 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 40/32 to yield 7.01 percent. The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 23 basis points from 26 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.

Both Candian and U.S. fixed-income markets rallied following reports showing U.S. durable goods orders fell more than expected in March, while the U.S. employment cost index for the first quarter rose less than expected.
The Canadian dollar rallied below C$1.40 (US$0.7143) on the news. The currency had been under pressure in recent weeks on concern about the possibility of a near-term U.S. rate rise.
In other prices, the Canadian 10-year benchmark bond rose C$1.10 to C$102.00 to yield 6.712 percent. The U.S. bond rose 28/32 to yield 6.78 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to seven basis points from five basis points on Monday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.14 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.32 percent.
